policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV names the ancestor as Elam, matching the qere/base reading עֵילָם rather than the ketiv עולם.
ASV 'As thou hast said' does not distinguish singular כדברך from plural כדבריך, and the mapped note is only an alternative_rendering.
ASV prints Jeremoth, matching ketiv ירמות; its mapped textual-variant note identifies Ramoth, the qere/base reading, as the alternative.
ASV prints Cheluhi, matching ketiv כלהי; its mapped textual-variant note identifies Cheluhu, the qere/base reading, as the alternative.
ASV prints Jaasu, matching ketiv ויעשו; its mapped textual-variant note identifies Jaasai, the qere/base reading, as the alternative.
ASV prints Iddo, matching ketiv ידו; its mapped textual-variant note identifies Jaddai, the qere/base reading, as the alternative.
ASV's main text 'had taken foreign wives' renders the plural verbal reading נשאו (qere/base); the mapped note is only an alternative_rendering and does not overturn that distinction.
